questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pairs form the same osazone?
questions.solution: During osazone formation (when sugars are reacted with phenylhydrazine) the reaction occurs at $\mathrm{C}_1$ and $\mathrm{C}_2$ while rest of the position remains intact. Since glucose and fructose differ from each other only in the arrangement of atom at $C_1$ and $C_2$, therefore they give the same osazone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is/are $\alpha$ - amino acid?
questions.solution: $\alpha$-amino acids are bifunctional organic compounds. They contain a basic amino group $\left(-\mathrm{NH}_{2}\right)$ on the $\alpha$-carbon and one acidic carboxyl group $(-\mathrm{COOH})$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Fructose reduces Tollen's reagent due to
options: enolisation of fructose followed by conversion to aldehyde by base
questions.solution:
In aqueous medium, fructose is enolised and converted into aldehyde in basic medium. Generally all aldehydes reduce Tollen's reagent, thus fructose can also reduces Tollen's 
reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many tripeptides can be prepared by linking the amino acids glycine, alanine and phenyl alanine?
questions.solution:
Tripeptides are amino acids polymers in which three individual amino acid units, called residues, are linked together by amide bonds. glycine $\left(\mathrm{NH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}\right)$, alanine
can be linked in six different ways.

questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.solution: Milk contains lactose as milk sugar. After digestion of milk lactose is broken down by enzymes lactase to form glucose and galactose before it enter the blood stream.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following sets consists only of essential amino acids?
questions.solution:
Out of 20 amino acids, the 10 amino acids which human body cannot synthesize are called essential amino acids. The ten essential amino acids are:
$1)$ Valine 2) Leucine 3) Isolucine 4) Histidine 5) Phenylanaline 6) Methionine 7 ) Tryptophan 8) Lysine 9 ) Arginine 10) Threonine.
